item.title: Live Updates: Trump tells GOP "we gave this a very strong shot"
item.description: President Trump held an event Monday at the Washington, D.C., Reflecting Pool, while Michigan Democrats assess the fallout from a cross-party endorsement.

item.title: Josh Turek pitches "generational change" in tight Iowa Senate race
item.description: In Iowa's crucial Senate race, Democrat Josh Turek pitched his campaign as an opportunity for a "generational change."

item.title: U.S. launches defensive strikes at Iranian targets
item.description: The U.S. military launched strikes at Iran after Iran fired at a U.S. aircraft, a senior U.S. official told CBS News.

item.title: New York congressional candidate Blake Gendebien talks about the cost of living ahead of midterms
item.description: Vice President JD Vance was in Rome, New York, on Monday campaigning on behalf of Republican congressional candidate Anthony Constantino in the state's 21st district. Democrat Blake Gendebien is challenging Constantino for Trump ally Elise Stefanik's seat. Gendebien joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Trump says "Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible"
item.description: President Trump must decide whether to end the war or return to it, Iran says, as both sides trade threats, but keep diplomacy alive.

item.title: Coast Guard detains cruise ship in Miami, officials say
item.description: The MSC Poesia cruise ship is currently detained with passengers on board at the Port of Miami, and its itinerary is currently on hold, Coast Guard officials tell CBS News.

item.title: ICE planning to deport Afghans through Pakistan, official says
item.description: The plan has triggered alarm among advocates for Afghans, who warn that the proposal could lead to the deportation of Afghans who could be persecuted by the Taliban.

item.title: More European grocery stores hit by apparent fridge-freezer hacks
item.description: Grocery chains in European nations say temperatures in some stores' fridges and freezers soared over 100 degrees just weeks after a similar incident in France.

item.title: Former Border Patrol chief says southern border is at quietest level he's ever seen
item.description: Former Border Patrol chief Raul Ortiz says some Biden administration officials were "embracing the chaos and crisis" at the southern border, but now he says the U.S.-Mexico border is at the quietest level he's ever seen.

item.title: Political AI deepfakes infiltrating midterm elections, could pose risks to voters
item.description: CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo discusses the issue of AI-generated deepfake videos in the lead-up to Election Day.

item.title: How Hispanic voters could sway midterm election outcomes
item.description: Hispanic Americans could be one of the most consequential voting blocks in Tuesday's midterm elections. Journalist Enrique Acevedo joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: GOP Senate candidate Ashley Hinson says she's "pro-Iowa" when asked if she's MAGA
item.description: Republican Senate candidate Rep. Ashley Hinson told CBS News she's an "Iowa common sense conservative" as she works to secure votes in her tight race with Democrat Josh Turek. CBS news' Lana Zak has more.

item.title: Michigan's Democratic Party chair says Haley Stevens "lied to her own constituents"
item.description: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens shocked her party this weekend when she endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for Senate over her primary opponent Abdul El-Sayed. The state's Democratic Party chair, Curtis Hertel Jr., joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: New cyberattacks hit supermarket fridges across Europe
item.description: Grocery store chains across Europe are scrambling to re-stock shelves after a cyberattack left massive amounts of food spoiled. CBS news international reporter Inaya Folarin Iman has more.

item.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's request in California mail ballots dispute
item.description: Earlier Monday, the Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to order California election officials to set aside mail ballots from 20,000 people it alleges are noncitizens.

item.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump request for California to set aside ballots from alleged noncitizens
item.description: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected President Trump's effort to set aside California ballots from 20,000 alleged noncitizens. CBS News' Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: ICE officer charged in Texas after allegedly hitting man with vehicle
item.description: A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer was charged with a felony for allegedly hitting a man with a vehicle earlier this month.

item.title: How Kalshi traders reacted to Haley Stevens' endorsement of Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: CBS News' Anthony Salvanto and Kalshi's head of research Nicole Kagan join "The Takeout" to discuss how Kalshi traders are spending their money with one day left until the midterm elections. Kalshi is a prediction market sponsor of CBS News.

item.title: 109-year-old best friends share key to long, happy lives: "Just be kind to people"
item.description: Two 109-year-old best friends, who met during the Roosevelt administration, say exercise, eating right and kindness are the keys to living long and happy lives. Tony Dokoupil has their story.

item.title: Massachusetts prosecutors intend to retry Lindsay Clancy
item.description: Massachusetts prosecutors said they intend to try Lindsay Clancy again, nearly two months after her murder trial resulted in a hung jury. She was on trial for the killings of her three young children. Shanelle Kaul reports from Plymouth.

item.title: ICE officer turns himself in after allegedly running down immigrant with SUV
item.description: An ICE officer turned himself in on Monday after being indicted on an assault charge in Texas for allegedly running down an immigrant with his SUV, leaving the man, who had been in the state for decades, hospitalized for weeks. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: Last-minute polls show Democrats leading in Ohio Senate and gubernatorial races
item.description: A new New York Times/Siena poll shows Democrats with an edge in Ohio's races for senator and governor. Nina Turner, former Ohio Democratic state senator and co-chair of Bernie Sanders' 2020 presidential campaign, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Trump touts renovation projects instead of addressing cost of living in final midterm push
item.description: President Trump made his final pitch to voters from the Reflecting Pool in Washington, D.C., on Monday. He held up photos of his various renovation projects, rather than take on cost-of-living issues, which voters say matter to them most. Weijia Jiang has more details on his closing pitch and Ed O'Keefe has the races to watch on Election Day.

item.title: Details on the races to watch heading into the 2026 midterm elections
item.description: "The Takeout" breaks down the top races as voters head to the polls in the 2026 midterm elections.

item.title: 11/2: CBS Evening News
item.description: President Trump makes his closing midterm pitch to voters; a Texas ICE officer was charged with aggravated assault.

item.title: Pilot in plane crash said "we're managing the ice," then "Mayday"
item.description: The business jet crashed onto a busy road, killing all nine people on board the aircraft as it burst into a massive fireball and left a huge crater.

item.title: 11/2: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Fallout continues after Haley Stevens' endorsement of Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate race; Candidates make final pitches ahead of midterms.

item.title: Snap settles social media addiction lawsuit, averting trial
item.description: Snap joins Alphabet, Meta and TikTok in resolving allegations that its social media platform was designed to encourage addictive behavior.

item.title: Trump says Iran war will be put away very soon, "one way or the other"
item.description: Earlier, President Trump predicted the war with Iran is "going to end soon," without offering any details, as Qatari mediators return to Tehran to push for a deal.

item.title: Judge tosses lawsuit seeking to delay certification of Alaska Senate race
item.description: The Justice Department argued that Daniel J. Sullivan's name on the ballot potentially diverted voters, and the Democrat running in the race would benefit as a result.
